page_title: Papilot · A Modern Agentic LaTeX Editor

sources.entry: Papilot - Open-source desktop app where you annotate the compiled PDF, run coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor in isolated Git worktrees, and review rendered before-and-after PDF diffs before merging. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/PapilotAI/papilot) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Papilot
summary.one_liner: Papilot is a free, open-source desktop and command-line LaTeX editor where AI coding agents edit the source and you review each change as a typeset before-and-after PDF diff.
use_cases: Reviewing AI-suggested edits to a LaTeX paper before they are merged
Annotating a compiled PDF to tell an agent what to change
Running several coding agents on separate paper edits in isolated Git worktrees
Editing an academic paper with AI while keeping a Git history of changes
Checking how equation or figure edits render before accepting them
summary.what_it_does:
Papilot lets you select a sentence, equation, or figure on the compiled PDF and write the change you want. It passes the exact source lines to a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, so you do not need to locate the file yourself. Each agent task runs in its own Git worktree. Every proposed change is shown as a typeset before-and-after PDF, and nothing is applied to the paper until you accept it; you can also comment to have the agent revise. Committing and pushing accepted changes is a separate step, so all changes remain in Git history. It is available as a desktop app and as a command-line tool installed via npm.</what_it_does>
